decisions.reason: Conferencing is a low-cost add-on close to the core offer, but it faces strong commoditised competition and has little reported traction, so the option stays open with moderate risk of abandonment.
Customer adoption by data centres and financial hubs is an early positive signal for an infrastructure-based product that fits the strategic direction, which justifies further commitment.
Optical spectrum fits the high-bandwidth, software-defined strategy, has its own page, and runs on owned fibre, so it is cheap to keep while demand uncertainty resolves.
A self-service number ordering portal supports the existing voice business at low marginal cost and fits the real-time provisioning direction, so keeping the option open is sensible.

Carrier pre-selection is a declining legacy telephony service in a shrinking market, but keeping it on existing infrastructure costs little, so it is kept for now with a notable chance of being dropped.
Direct voice connection (SIP-type) services are core to the enterprise voice business and cheap to maintain on the owned network, so there is no strong reason to abandon them.
